resolution.note:
Both refuters killed every blocking finding, so the row stamps PASS:verify-refuted and this REVISE stays as the record. slides §1 Referent resolution under a sequential deck read line 58: harm: The facts check out, but the harm does not. I confirmed that line 58 names no cases, that Mata v. Avianca and Deloitte/DEWR first appear on line 62 in the next chunk, and that the maintainer block has no accept-note for this line. The judge's account of the text is accurate, so I am refuting on harm, not on counting.

(a) Nobody in the room is worse off. "Bring to Module 5" is a homework hand-off, not a comprehension beat. The student cannot write "the missing organisational check was X" until they have read the cases, and the slide says where they are. The next slide, headed "Pre-reads before Module 5", names both cases in its first line and links "The Missing Check", whose title echoes the sentence the student must write. Under a sequential deck read the referent resolves one slide later, and the slide itself says so.

(b) The finding restates the rule more than it shows a consequence. check_slides.md §1 lists "never named, forward references included". Its example is a bare reference, "before the three things get named", that points at a later slide with no signal that it does. Line 58 is a different shape. "Both cases are in the pre-reads that follow" is an explicit reading-order pointer, which the same compendium's §12 endorses ("that follow" survives projection). The reader is told the referent is coming and where. It is not left with nothing to resolve.

(c) and (d) The fix is a near no-op with side costs. Line 62 already carries the names, so adding them to line 58 puts the same names on two adjacent slides. That is the doctrine-restatement problem §16 calls a cut class. It also pushes against the maintainer's red-thread note of 2026-11-13: "Align existing lines; add none." The judge argues it adds names and no sentence. It still lengthens a bolded hand-off line that is meant to stay a short assignment.

(e) Blame and history. Line 58 was reworded on 2026-11-13 and its earlier form was already a forward pointer. Commit 149d513c shows the prior text, "Both cases are named in the pre-reads that follow." The earlier slides judge (4d9c4af2) passed this file with that shape. Any new harm would have to come from the November wording, and that wording only dropped "named", which does not change what the reader can resolve.

Net: a tidiness point, with a no-op fix that duplicates line 62.
